request.tone: mystery and suspense; scariness moderate, peril moderate, violence mild
request.note: catalog book, read by a blind extractor; no request exists

pitch.hero: Wren Callahan, a sleepless teenager listening to her late grandfather's attic radio
pitch.want: to find who sends a looping number signal and answer him before it ends
pitch.obstacle: a countdown to 23:40, a gale and spring tide, and a failing power cell at the old relay station
pitch.stake: a lonely old man's thirty-year message to his daughter, and thirty years of tape, lost tonight
pitch.ending_kind: branching mystery: many setbacks, and several reunions or rescues that differ in who carries the message

wren.name: Wren Callahan
wren.want: to learn who is sending the loop and answer him before it ends tonight
wren.voice: third person present; practical, tired, brave, careful with her hands and her notes

alder.name: Kell Alder
alder.role: operator of Relay KX; sender of the loop
alder.want: to keep a channel open until his daughter answers
alder.voice: old, gruff and gentle; speaks in plain sentences and says child

marin.name: Marin Alder
marin.role: Alder's estranged daughter; the M of the loop
marin.want: to be asked home without having to speak first
marin.voice: careful vowels; heard only by telephone and radio

grandpa.name: Grandpa Callahan
grandpa.role: Wren's late grandfather; ham radio operator
grandpa.want: to reach Alder quietly and keep him from giving up
grandpa.voice: cramped square capitals in notes and letters

okafor.name: Mrs. Okafor
okafor.role: net mender at the marina; keeper of the pier card
okafor.want: to see the loop answered without handing out a man's grief
okafor.voice: slow, sharp, speaks in pauses over her needle

pell.name: Mr. Pell
pell.want: to point without naming a name
pell.voice: kind and wry, speaks in sea idiom

ruiz.name: Ruiz
ruiz.role: relay man who stayed; offstage helper
ruiz.want: to make up thirty years of silence with Alder

truth.statement: The loop is Kell Alder's thirty-year message to his estranged daughter Marin, the M of the two long tones: he swore to keep a channel open until she answered. The station's one aging power cell will fail and the tape will erase tonight at 23:40, with the spring tide and a gale arriving, so tonight is the last chance. Marin has been listening in secret all along, and Wren can reunite them or let it end.
truth.question: Who is sending the numbers, who is M, and what happens when the count runs out?

wren_listens_nightly.text: Wren Callahan cannot sleep and has listened to her grandfather's attic radio every night for a week.

grandpa_radio_attic.text: Wren's late grandfather's shortwave radio sits under a dust sheet in the attic.

grandpa_dead.text: Wren's grandfather is dead; he died about a year ago.

loop_signal.text: The radio carries a loop: a flat careful woman's voice reading numbers, then a slow tone that counts downward and resets.

grandpa_battery_shelf.text: Grandpa's spare battery, wrapped in a rag and labeled JUST IN CASE in his capitals, sits on the shelf above the radio.

grandpa_headset_hook.text: Grandpa's operator headset, name Callahan inked inside the band, hangs on a hook by the shelf; he swore it let you hear the room behind a voice.

bargain_one_thing.text: Wren allows herself to take down only one of her grandfather's two things.

wren_has_battery.text: Wren has taken Grandpa's spare battery from the shelf and carries it in her pack.

wren_has_headset.text: Wren has taken Grandpa's headset from its hook and wears it to listen.

headset_voice_close.text: Through the headset the hiss is deeper and the woman's voice sounds very close.

grandpa_logbook_forty_years.text: Grandpa kept a logbook of everything he heard on the radio, every night for forty years.

numbers_maybe_coordinates.text: Wren could plot the numbers as coordinates on graph paper, as her grandfather taught her.

relay_station_dark.text: The relay station on the headland has stood dark for as long as Wren remembers, and every kid in town thinks it is dead.

coord_harbor_tower_pairs.text: Two coordinate pairs from the numbers fall on the working harbor and on the old water tower on the ridge, a mile and a half apart.

wren_handheld_radio.text: Wren carries a handheld radio that plays the loop.

harbor_sites.text: The harbor has a harbormaster's hut with one lit window, a tide-gauge shed at the breakwater and a pier notice-board.

pier_card.text: A fresh index card pinned in the middle of the pier notice-board gives the loop's frequency and the words: if you hear the loop, it is real.

card_freq_matches_loop.text: The frequency on the pier card matches the loop exactly, and the ink is still damp.

card_replaced_regularly.text: Somebody replaces the pier card each time it blows away, and has done so for years.

signal_north_headland.text: Tuned to the card's frequency, the loop is loudest to the north along the shore toward the headland.

wren_has_pier_card.text: Wren has taken the pier card.

mr_pell_harbormaster.text: Mr. Pell is the harbormaster, a man in a cable-knit sweater who knows the old relay.

pell_headland_relay.text: Mr. Pell says the loop used to come from the old relay on the headland and that someone stubborn has kept it going.

loop_from_headland_relay.text: The loop comes from the old relay station on the headland.

county_closed_station.text: The county closed the relay station and pulled its money and staff.

shed_receiver_inside.text: The tide-gauge shed, supposedly dead for years, holds a small receiver blinking in time with the loop.

tide_shed_ear_relay_kx.text: The shed receiver is solar powered and is only an ear for a signal sent from further out by a station called Relay KX.

station_called_kx.text: The relay station is called Relay KX.

grandpa_tick_on_dial.text: Grandpa marked the loop's frequency with a pencil tick on the radio dial and listened to it for years without telling anyone.

tower_catches_signal.text: The rust-red ridge water tower catches the signal and throws it on; its ladder is flaking and its service box has a thick cable.

tower_repeater_cable_to_relay.text: The water tower is only a repeater; a cable runs from its antenna along the ridge to the headland relay.

ridge_arrows_path.text: Faded stenciled arrows with reflective tips mark a path along the ridge toward the headland.

station_lit_occupied.text: The relay station is not dark: a red lamp burns on its mast and one window of the low building is lit yellow.

wren_at_station_window.text: Wren stands outside the lit window of the station building at night, her back to the wall.

relay_gate_paths.text: At the chained station gate a cliff-top footpath follows the fence and a service lane runs behind the buildings.

fence_gap_cliff.text: The fence has peeled back from a post on the cliff path, leaving a gap, and the mast stands clear from there.

compound_maintained.text: The compound is kept up: weeds cut, new cable under a tarpaulin, a generator running.

man_lives_at_station.text: A man lives at the station; a yellow window shows a man holding a mug.

lane_buildings.text: On the service lane stand a gatehouse with a lit window, a humming transformer hut and cellar steps running into water.

cellar_floods_waves.text: Each wave against the sea wall sends more water down the cellar steps.

kx_promise_note.text: A note in a plastic sleeve in the cellar reads LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, signed KX.

wren_has_kx_note.text: Wren has taken the plastic sleeve and note from the cellar.

gatehouse_log_board.text: The warm gatehouse has a log board covered in years of entries in one careful hand, the last one only hours old.

dog_patrols_station.text: A man with a dog patrols the station grounds at night.

loop_holding_no_answer.text: The log board's last forty lines read LOOP HOLDING, STILL NO ANSWER.

person_tends_signal.text: A person tends the signal night after night and waits for an answer that never comes.

m_message_for_m.text: The newest log page reads FOR M, STILL HOLDING: the loop is a message for someone called M.

wren_has_log_page.text: Wren has taken the newest log page.

alder_serviced_hut.text: A sticker on the transformer hut shows a technician K. Alder has serviced it every month for years and still comes.

station_swept_step.text: The station building's step is swept and boots stand on it, so someone lives and works there.

grandpa_trunk_and_shed.text: Grandpa kept valued things in a cedar trunk in the attic and unfinished work in his radio shed, where a wall of his notes still hangs.

trunk_contents.text: The cedar trunk holds Grandpa's logbook, a bundle of QSL cards and a ribbon-tied stack of unstamped envelopes.

letters_to_kx_unposted.text: Grandpa wrote years of unstamped letters to a man called Kell at Relay KX on the headland and never posted them.

letter_she_may_be_out_there.text: A letter begins: Kell, she may still be out there, so keep the channel open.

kell_alder_operator_headland.text: The man at the headland relay is the operator Kell Alder.

grandpa_urged_alder_daughter.text: Grandpa's letters urge Alder not to give up on his own daughter and tell him somebody hears him every night.

thirty_envelopes.text: The bundle holds thirty unposted envelopes.

grandpa_knew_alder.text: Grandpa knew an operator named Alder was keeping the headland relay alive, listened to him for years and never told anyone.

wren_has_grandpa_letter.text: Wren has kept the top letter from the bundle.

grandpa_wanted_letters_delivered.text: Grandpa's pencil note on the last envelope says to take the letters out to KX by hand so Alder knows somebody heard.

logbook_tracks_kx_alder.text: Grandpa's logbook tracks the KX loop for years and keeps asking ALDER STILL TRANSMITTING, WHY.

club_wont_talk_alder.text: Nobody at the radio club will talk about Alder.

grandpa_unfinished_question.text: Grandpa's last logbook page, dated the week he died, asks whether anybody will answer the poor man.

wren_has_grandpa_logbook.text: Wren has Grandpa's logbook in her hands.

qsl_listener_cards.text: The QSL cards are forty years of confirmations from coastal listeners, in no order.

kx_alder_call_sign.text: One heavier QSL card names the call sign KX ALDER, underlined twice in Grandpa's hand.

three_cards_kx_alder_freq.text: Three cards name RELAY KX, HEADLAND, operator Alder, on the loop's exact frequency, and Grandpa logged the signal for thousands of nights.

nobody_answers_alder.text: In forty years of cards, no listener ever answered Alder on the air.

m_card_eleven_years.text: An eleven-year-old card signed M says: Heard KX again tonight, please do not tell him.

tuning_notes_wall.text: Hundreds of Grandpa's tuning notes are pinned across the radio shed wall.

grandpa_cabinet_letters.text: Grandpa kept his letters in a padlocked steel filing cabinet in the radio shed.

grandpa_tuning_note_alder.text: A pinned note reads KX LOOP, HEADLAND RELAY, OPERATOR ALDER, DO NOT GIVE UP ON HIM; Alder never answers and Grandpa meant to keep trying.

grandpa_two_dots_slip.text: A slip hidden behind the cabinet drawer reads KX, EVERY MIDNIGHT, TWO DOTS, NO REPLY YET.

alder_license_kx.text: A framed license names Kell Alder of Station KX.

alder_thirty_logbooks.text: Thirty year-labelled logbooks stand on Alder's shelf; he has sat at the station every night for thirty years.

station_room_contents.text: The station room holds a console of dials, two turning tape reels, a desk chair and a steaming mug.

alder_sends_loop.text: Kell Alder is a person who sends the loop out every night from the station; it is no machine left running by mistake.

wren_left_note.text: Wren wedged a note reading I HEAR YOU, signed W, in the station door frame.

flashlight_stops_at_door.text: The flashlight stops at the door and stays perfectly still for a long time.

alder_unaware_of_wren.text: Alder never knew Wren was at his window.

alder_tall_stooped.text: Alder is a tall stooped figure.

county_site_decommissioned.text: The county website says the relay station was decommissioned thirty years ago and has no staff.

wren_corkboard.text: Wren has a corkboard over her desk with copied numbers, a map of the headland and a card reading KELL ALDER, KX.

wren_has_loop_recording.text: Wren has a recording of the loop to time and decode.

numbers_may_be_time.text: The loop's groups arrive on a beat that is not quite steady, so the numbers might count time rather than spell words.

grandpa_tide_table.text: Grandpa's battered, underlined tide table is in Wren's room.

cipher_fragments.text: Treating the numbers as a book cipher on the logbook yields HOLDING, ANSWER and a recurring M, but one cluster fails.

loop_decoded.text: The numbers decode to STILL HOLDING THE CHANNEL OPEN FOR M, followed by a figure that shrinks from night to night.

loop_has_count_down.text: The broadcast includes a count that is going down.

tide_key_cluster_date_hour.text: The tide table as key turns the stubborn cluster into a date and an hour, and turns the rest into rubbish.

loop_ends_2340_tonight.text: The loop's countdown ends tonight at 23:40.

intervals_shrinking.text: The gaps between cycles of the loop shrink by a regular amount.

countdown_ends_tonight.text: The loop's countdown runs out tonight, a little before midnight.

countdown_points_today_rough.text: Wren's rough figures on the calendar close in on today, though her method is untested.

m_in_loop.text: The letter M recurs in the loop.

okafor_net_mender.text: Mrs. Okafor mends nets at the marina, has watched the headland since before the relay was built, and remembers everything but repeats little.

library_microfilm.text: The county library keeps a hundred years of the local paper on microfilm and closes at seven.

microfilm_relay_closure_article.text: The microfilm carries a story and photograph about the county closing the relay, with one man standing apart.

alder_senior_operator_refused.text: Kell Alder was the relay's senior operator and the only one of nine staff who refused the transfer inland, thirty years ago.

alder_quote_channel_open.text: Alder told the reporter that somebody has to keep the channel open.

alder_caption_the_one_who_would_not_go.text: A caption reads K. Alder, senior operator, the one who would not go.

letter_editor_poor_man.text: A letter to the editor from eleven years later complains the relay hums at night and that somebody should tell that poor man nobody is listening.

okafor_pins_card.text: Mrs. Okafor has pinned a card to the pier board every month for thirty years saying the loop is real; Wren is the first who came.

alder_daughter_quarrel.text: Alder had a daughter; they had a quarrel the whole harbor heard and she took the morning bus and never wrote.

alder_swore_channel.text: Alder swore before witnesses to keep a channel open until his daughter answered.

okafor_told_wren_ring_marina.text: Wren told Mrs. Okafor the truth about the attic radio, and Mrs. Okafor told her to ring the marina day or night if the loop looks like stopping.

alder_kept_girl_voice_thirty_years.text: A man has kept a girl's voice on the air for thirty years, as Mrs. Okafor hints.

morse_chart_lid.text: A Morse chart is taped inside the lid of the attic radio.

loop_two_tones_spell_m.text: The loop opens with two long tones, dash dash, which are the Morse letter M.

loop_gap_waiting.text: After the falling tone the loop leaves a four-second gap of open air: the sender names someone, says his piece and waits for an answer.

numbers_voice_is_daughter.text: An old recording under the voice shows the woman reading the numbers was once a girl who called the station operator Dad.

loop_degrading_nightly.text: Each night the loop's falling tone starts lower and its closing gap is shorter, so the loop is running out of room.

grandpa_marine_chart.text: Grandpa's marine chart of the headland lies rolled on Wren's desk, its margins crowded with letters for moorings and markers.

marin_is_alders_daughter.text: Marin is Kell Alder's only child, his daughter.

marin_vanished_thirty_years.text: Marin vanished from every local register thirty years ago with no forwarding address.

alder_sister_near_harbor.text: Alder's sister is still living three streets from the harbor, with the same telephone number.

m_is_marin.text: The M in the loop stands for Marin.

marin_read_numbers_for_father.text: Marin used to read the station numbers for her father, and after a row she left.

loop_is_apology_to_marin.text: The loop is an apology and a call to Marin to come home.

marin_cannot_hear_loop.text: Marin has spent thirty years somewhere the loop cannot reach her.

sister_stopped_listening.text: Alder's sister could once hear the loop, stopped listening years ago and is ashamed.

marin_last_address_west.text: Marin's last known address is in a town two ridges west where nobody has answered a card in years.

chart_ringed_m.text: On the chart a pencil M ringed twice marks a mooring just inside the breakwater, with a date thirty years old.

marin_mooring_kept.text: A brass plate on the old mooring buoy chained to the harbor wall reads Marin and HER MOORING IS KEPT.

evening_forecast.text: The evening forecast has been muttering about the headland all day.

archive_documents.text: The county archive has two documents on the relay, a maintenance sheet and an operating schedule, and Wren has printed both.

station_single_cell.text: The relay runs on one sealed power cell installed the year the county left, never replaced and eleven years past its rated life.

count_is_cell_life.text: The count is Alder's measure of how long his station's power cell has left to live.

station_final_schedule_erase.text: The operating schedule's FINAL entry reads PLAY TAPE 2, THEN ERASE ALL, dated tonight at 23:40 after three postponements.

spring_tide_high_2342.text: Tonight's spring tide, the biggest of the month, peaks at 23:42.

gale_warning_eleven.text: The forecast carries a gale warning for the headland from eleven o'clock.

tide_floods_yard.text: With the gale behind it, the sea will stand in the station yard tonight.

count_zero_as_tide_drowns.text: The station will be drowned by the tide at the very minute the count reaches zero.

tide_knocked_out_relay.text: The tide knocked out the power at the relay station.

news_no_broadcast_thirty_years.text: The news reporter says nobody has broadcast from the relay in thirty years.

loop_stopped_before_wren_acted.text: The loop stopped for good before Wren found the man sending it.

alder_last_tape_to_marin.text: Alder recorded a last tape addressed to his daughter Marin: he will say his piece at the end of the final hour and then let her be.

loop_one_hour_left.text: The loop has one hour left to run and this time the count will not start over.

cell_cannot_carry_schedule.text: The station's power cell will not carry another schedule, so this one is the last.

alder_kept_note_for_w.text: Alder found Wren's note, walked the fence twice looking for its writer, kept the paper in his shirt pocket and recorded a message thanking W.

alder_spending_last_hour_on_marin.text: Alder has chosen to spend the station's last hour talking to someone who left.

grandpa_transmitter_dust_sheet.text: Grandpa's transmitter sits under a dust sheet in the attic.

wren_alone_one_hour.text: Nobody else knows; Wren has fifty-nine minutes, a bicycle, the transmitter and a telephone.

station_yard_flooded.text: The station yard has turned to a sheet of black water ruffled by the gale.

door_ajar_lit.text: A door stands ajar across the open yard with warm light spilling out, and a longer sheltered route runs behind the sheds.

control_room_empty.text: The control room is warm and empty, with a mug still steaming by the microphone.

console_red_countdown.text: Red numbers on the console count down.

tape_after_last_send_erase.text: A strip of tape under the countdown reads AFTER LAST SEND, ERASE.

hold_switch_guarded.text: A guarded switch marked HOLD sits at the center of the console.

circled_number_address_book.text: An address book beside the telephone has one number circled so many times the paper shines.

power_cell_dying.text: The station's power cell gutters in a rusted housing, and the red numbers dim whenever it dips.

alder_outside_mast_cable.text: Somebody with a flashlight is fighting a loose cable at the foot of the mast.

last_message_then_erase_plan.text: Alder means to send his last message once and then erase thirty years of tape.

patch_cord_phone_console.text: A patch cord runs from the desk telephone into the console.

circled_number_is_marins.text: The circled number is Marin's, the one person the last message was always meant for.

hold_stops_send_and_erase.text: The HOLD switch would stop both the sending and the erasing.

second_cell_terminals.text: Beside the dying cell two bare terminals wait for a second cell, and a fresh battery clipped across them would carry the station for hours.

grandpa_taught_clip_colors.text: Grandpa showed Wren how to clip red to red and black to black on a camping lantern when she was nine.

radio_club_night_number_phone.text: The radio club's night number is taped to the station telephone.

station_powered_hours.text: With the spare battery spliced in, the station will not die for hours.

radio_club_arrives.text: The radio club's night operator sends trucks and a generator to the gate.

marin_two_ridges_west.text: Marin lives in a town two ridges west.

marin_answers_phone.text: Marin answers the telephone and hears her father's message or voice.

word_marin_recorded_on_phone.text: Wren's phone recorded the single word Marin from Alder's tape.

alder_at_console_headset.text: Alder, an old man in a heavy headset, sits at the console with his back to the window.

door_bolted_inside.text: The steel back door is bolted on the inside.

alder_believes_marin_not_listening.text: Alder believes Marin is not listening and has stopped pretending she is.

alder_only_saying_goodbye.text: Alder says tonight he is only saying goodbye.

alder_speaks_live.text: For the first time in thirty years Alder speaks live to Marin with nothing recorded between them.

marin_has_been_listening.text: Marin has been listening all along without answering.

attic_eight_miles.text: Wren heard Alder from an attic eight miles away.

others_promised_alder.text: For ten years the harbormaster, the minister and Alder's sister promised him Marin was listening.

grandpa_two_dots_twenty_years.text: Grandpa sent two dots every midnight for twenty years, which Alder took for a fault in his set.

alder_kept_marin_voice_on_air.text: Alder kept Marin's voice on the air so she would always know the way home.

grandpa_never_let_wren_key.text: Grandpa never let Wren key his transmitter, since it needs a license, but she watched him for years.

club_card_net_line.text: Grandpa's club card on the wall carries the county radio net's emergency line.

wren_knows_keying_steps.text: Wren knows the steps: main switch, warm the valves, tune for the dip, watch the needle.

needle_pencil_mark.text: Grandpa kept the transmitter's power needle at a quarter of its scale beside a pencil mark.

red_band_forbidden.text: The power knob turns past the pencil mark into a red band Grandpa never let it touch.

bare_carrier_answer.text: Someone out there keys a bare carrier in answer to Wren's calls for Marin.

marin_answers_on_radio.text: Marin answers on the radio, older than the voice reading the numbers but with the same careful vowels.

county_net_relays_message.text: The county radio net repeats a message for Marin Alder on every station's frequency.

transmitter_burned_out.text: The overpowered transmitter pops, smokes and burns out after ten seconds on the air.

net_recorded_menu.text: The net's line plays a recording: press one if life or property is in danger, otherwise leave a message heard at six.

duty_controller_knows_kx.text: The duty controller knows Kell's KX and takes the call seriously.

woman_west_no_callsign.text: A woman two ridges west with no call sign keeps asking what the message says.

marin_read_numbers_at_seventeen.text: Marin read the numbers for her father at seventeen and has listened for thirty years without touching the key.

stations_repeat_hourly.text: Twenty-three stations promise to repeat the message for Marin at the top of every hour.

marin_asks_after_station.text: A listener two ridges west has asked after KX every winter for eleven years and never left her name.

coast_guard_aux_number.text: The coast guard auxiliary's number is printed along the bottom of the tide table.

grandpa_address_book_relay_men.text: Grandpa's address book lists men who worked the relay, under K for KX.

okafor_has_station_key.text: Mrs. Okafor carries a key to the station's back door on twine, given by Alder after thirty years of her leaving soup on his step.

alder_has_had_number_six_years.text: Alder has had Marin's number in his address book for six years.

crew_chief_at_station.text: A coast guard auxiliary crew chief and crew reach the station with sandbags and a generator.

eight_staff_transferred.text: Grandpa's address book brackets eight relay staff as TRANSFERRED INLAND with distant numbers.

ruiz_stayed.text: Ruiz, a relay man who stayed across the bay, is marked in Grandpa's book STAYED, WON'T TALK.

ruiz_has_keys.text: Ruiz still has his keys to the station and has long watched its mast lamp.

ruiz_splices_cell.text: Ruiz strips a spare cell from the mast heater and wires it across the dying one.

ruiz_watches_lamp.text: Ruiz watches the mast lamp from his kitchen across the bay every night.

n_open.event: Wren climbs to the attic and listens again to the looping voice and falling tone on her late grandfather's radio.

n_shelf.event: Wren eyes two untouched things of her grandfather's and sets herself a one-thing rule.

n_shelf_battery.event: Wren takes down the spare battery and packs it in her bag.

n_shelf_headset.event: Wren lifts the headset off its hook and hears the voice very close.

n_start.event: Three leads pull at Wren: plot the numbers, bike to the relay, or hunt for the logbook.

r_coord_1.event: Wren plots the numbers and finds two coordinate pairs on the harbor and the ridge water tower.

r_coord_harbor.event: At the sleeping harbor Wren chooses between the hut, the shed and the notice-board.

r_coord_notice.event: On the notice-board Wren finds a fresh card with the loop's frequency and a message.

r_coord_notice2.event: The card matches the loop and its ink is damp; Wren must take it or leave it for its intended reader.

r_coord_notice3.event: Wren takes the card, tunes to its frequency and finds the signal strongest northward.

e_coord_notice.event: Wren leaves the card; it is replaced, nobody comes, and the loop ends while she waits.

r_coord_harbor_ask.event: Mr. Pell says the loop used to come from the old headland relay and points her there without naming anyone.

r_coord_harbor_shed.event: A receiver blinks in time with the loop inside the tide-gauge shed; the door is swollen.

r_coord_shed_in.event: Wren shoves the door and finds the receiver is an ear for a station called Relay KX further out.

e_coord_shed_leave.event: Wren copies the frequency and goes home; Grandpa's pencil tick marks the same dial spot and the loop dies by the weekend.

r_coord_tower.event: At the rust-red water tower Wren faces a flaking ladder up and a service box below.

r_coord_climb.event: Wren climbs eight rungs, freezes, then sees a cable running along the ridge toward the relay.

r_coord_base.event: At the service box Wren finds stenciled arrows leading along the ridge.

r_coord_base_in.event: Prying the box open shows a tag KX RELAY, HEADLAND; the tower is only a repeater.

r_coord_base_out.event: Wren follows nineteen reflective arrows along the ridge road as the loop steadies.

r_coord_beat.event: Along the moonlit headland track Wren realizes the numbers point out to the relay on the point.

r_coord_close.event: Wren finds the relay lit, slips in by the cliff side and crouches by the window.

r_relay_1.event: Wren bikes to the chained gate and chooses the cliff path or the sheltered service lane.

r_re_path.event: The windy cliff path shows a gap in the fence and a clear view of the mast.

r_re_gap.event: Wren slips through the gap and finds a signed, well-kept compound with a running generator.

e_re_photo.event: Wren photographs the mast and goes home; the third picture shows a man with a mug and the loop dies two nights later.

r_re_lane.event: On the flooded service lane Wren sees a gatehouse, a humming hut and cellar steps.

r_re_cellar.event: Wren wades down into the rising cellar and sees a taped sleeve whose first word is LOOP.

r_re_cellar2.event: The note reads LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, signed KX, as the water climbs to her knees.

r_re_cellar3.event: Wren rips the note off the wall, escapes a surge soaked and pockets the sleeve.

e_re_cellar.event: Wren flees the cellar and loses the sleeve; she has the words but falls ill for three days and the loop is gone.

r_re_gatehouse.event: The warm gatehouse holds a years-long log board as a dog approaches.

r_re_log.event: Wren reads LOOP HOLDING, STILL NO ANSWER and realizes a person tends the signal, as a man leads his dog away.

r_re_scrap.event: Wren takes the newest page, FOR M, STILL HOLDING, and runs.

r_re_hut.event: The hut's sticker shows a technician K. Alder has serviced it every month for years.

r_relay_beat.event: In the rain Wren sees the one lit window and swept step and concludes the loop's source is inside.

r_relay_close.event: Wren crosses the yard unchallenged to the lit window; boots on the step mean a person.

r_notes_1.event: Wren looks for Grandpa's logbook in the attic trunk or his radio shed.

r_no_trunk.event: The trunk holds a logbook, QSL cards and unstamped envelopes.

r_no_letters.event: Wren opens the envelopes, all addressed to Relay KX and written to a man called Kell.

r_no_letters2.event: The letter names Kell Alder, operator at the headland relay, and pleads with him not to give up on his daughter.

r_no_letters3.event: Wren reads more letters, all telling Alder somebody hears him and his girl may be listening, and keeps the top one.

e_no_letters.event: Wren reties and leaves the letters; later Grandpa's pencil note says to deliver them to KX by hand but the loop is gone.

r_no_book.event: The logbook tracks the KX loop for years and ends asking whether anybody will answer the poor man.

r_no_cards.event: The QSL cards include a heavier one naming KX ALDER underlined twice.

r_no_freq.event: Three cards name RELAY KX, operator Alder, on the loop's exact frequency; nobody ever answered him.

e_no_cards_end.event: Wren sorts the cards till three, finds an eleven-year-old M card, and the loop goes quiet two days later.

r_no_shed.event: The radio shed has a wall of tuning notes and a padlocked cabinet.

r_no_tuning.event: A circled note reads KX LOOP, OPERATOR ALDER, DO NOT GIVE UP ON HIM.

e_no_locked.event: Wren topples the cabinet, is caught by her mother, and finds a slip reading KX, EVERY MIDNIGHT, TWO DOTS, NO REPLY YET.

r_notes_beat.event: Wren reflects that Grandpa knew someone kept the headland station alive and never told a soul.

r_notes_close.event: Wren bikes the headland road, ducks through the fence and finds the relay lit.

n_b1.event: Through the window Wren sees Kell Alder's console, tapes, mug and thirty logbooks as a flashlight approaches.

n_b1_note.event: Wren wedges a note reading I HEAR YOU, signed W, in the door frame and flees as the flashlight stops at it.

n_b1_slip.event: Wren backs away unseen and watches a tall stooped figure sit down at the desk.

n_b1_echo.event: Wren pins KELL ALDER, KX on her corkboard; the county says the station was decommissioned thirty years ago.

n_b1_choice.event: Wren weighs cracking the numbers against asking the town about Kell Alder.

m_numbers_1.event: Wren copies the numbers and weighs a book cipher against timing the beats.

m_num_cipher.event: The book cipher gives fragments HOLDING, ANSWER, M then stalls on one cluster.

m_num_cracked.event: Shifting the logbook key one page decodes STILL HOLDING THE CHANNEL OPEN FOR M and a shrinking figure.

m_num_book2.event: The tide table decodes the stubborn cluster as a date and hour but gibbers on the rest.

m_num_cracked2.event: Trusting the one date and hour shows a clock set for tonight at 23:40.

e_num_gibberish.event: Wren grinds the tide key over the whole string until 1:10 a.m.; the loop has stopped and the date and hour were the whole message.

m_num_time.event: Timing eleven cycles with a stopwatch shows the gaps shrinking regularly.

m_num_intervals.event: A graph of the shrinking gaps reaches zero tonight a little before midnight.

m_num_pattern.event: Rough figures on the calendar close on today, but Wren doubts her own method.

m_num_countdown.event: Wren circles today's date: the loop is a countdown ending tonight.

e_num_giveup.event: Testing the method on static also yields a date; Wren is brushing her teeth at 23:40 when the loop ends with a man's single word.

m_who_1.event: Wren weighs the library microfilm against Mrs. Okafor at the marina.

m_who_film.event: The microfilm shows the relay closing and a photograph of one man standing apart; the library is closing soon.

m_who_article.event: The article says Alder was the only one of nine staff to refuse transfer and quotes him: somebody has to keep the channel open.

m_who_photo.event: Wren photographs pages; two matter: Alder's caption and a letter saying someone should tell that poor man nobody is listening.

m_who_okafor.event: Mrs. Okafor demands to know why Wren asks about Alder before she says a word.

m_who_story.event: Wren tells the truth; Okafor reveals Alder's daughter, the quarrel and the vow, and says ring the marina if the loop stops.

e_who_warn.event: Wren says it is a school project; Okafor refuses and hints at the voice, leaving Wren with a worse question.

n_b2.event: Wren decodes the two long tones as M and realizes the four-second gap is the sender waiting.

n_b2_under.event: With the headset Wren hears an old recording under the voice: a girl calling the station operator Dad.

n_b2_echo.event: Wren logs the loop and sees the starting note lower and the gap shorter each night.

n_b2_choice.event: Wren chooses between finding who M is and finding what the count runs down to.

mm_listener_1.event: Wren considers whether M is a person or a place.

mm_list_family.event: Records show Kell Alder's only child Marin and his sister, still living near the harbor.

mm_list_daughter.event: Online scraps show Marin read the numbers for her father; the loop is an apology she cannot hear.

mm_list_sister.event: Alder's sister confirms M is Marin, the quarrel, and gives Marin's last address two ridges west.

mm_list_place.event: The chart has an M ringed twice beside a breakwater mooring, dated thirty years ago.

mm_list_map.event: A brass plate on the harbor buoy reads Marin, HER MOORING IS KEPT: M is a person.

e_list_deadend.event: Wren works the whole chart; the radio says one hour and then a man says a name once and the channel is empty.

mm_count_1.event: Wren can follow the falling line or check the count against the tide table and forecast.

mm_count_time.event: The falling line hits zero at 23:40 tonight; Wren has printed a maintenance sheet and an operating schedule.

mm_count_extrap.event: The maintenance sheet shows the relay's single power cell is eleven years past rated life; the count is its remaining life.

mm_count_clock.event: The operating schedule's FINAL line says PLAY TAPE 2, THEN ERASE ALL, dated tonight at 23:40 after three postponements.

mm_count_tide.event: The tide table and gale warning put a spring tide peaking at 23:42 over the station yard.

mm_count_warn.event: Wren trusts the tide: the station will be drowned the minute the count hits zero.

e_count_wait.event: Wren waits for daylight; the tide knocks out the relay's power and the news says nobody has broadcast there in thirty years.

n_b3.event: At 22:40 the loop pauses for a tape of Alder telling Marin it is the last schedule with one hour left.

n_b3_note.event: After the tape a second message thanks the W who left three words and says Alder kept the note.

n_b3_echo.event: Rain starts; Wren pictures the warm room and the man who can measure the death of his own station.

n_b3_choice.event: With 59 minutes left Wren weighs the bicycle, her grandfather's transmitter and the telephone.

f_station_1.event: Wren rides out; at the flooded gate with nine minutes left she picks the fence or the service road.

f_st_fence.event: Wren climbs into the flooded yard and chooses the open dash to a lit door or the longer sheltered way.

f_st_control.event: In the empty control room Wren sees the countdown, the ERASE tape, the HOLD switch, the circled number and the dying cell.

f_st_answer.event: Under two minutes, Wren understands Alder's plan and that dialing the circled number or throwing HOLD are her options.

f_st_power.event: The dying cell has two bare terminals for a second cell; Wren can splice a spare or nurse it by hand.

f_st_spliced.event: Wren splices in Grandpa's spare battery, steadying the station for hours, and can phone the club or throw HOLD then dial.

e_st_stabilize.event: The radio club hears Wren, trucks and a generator arrive, HOLD is thrown and a call goes west as Alder is fetched from the mast.

e_st_both.event: Wren throws HOLD at 41 seconds, rings Marin and plays Alder's tape; Alder arrives to hear his daughter say Dad.

e_st_reunite.event: Wren dials the circled number as the count hits zero; Alder's message plays to Marin and the tape erases as Alder arrives.

e_st_archive.event: Wren throws HOLD with eleven seconds left, saving the tapes, and Alder arrives and decides to stay.

e_st_record.event: Nursing the cell by hand, Wren hears Alder's tape say Marin before the cell dies; her phone records the one word.

e_st_hesitate.event: Wren detours behind the sheds, the lamp goes out and the reels wipe themselves; she is one minute too late to dial.

f_st_road.event: At the sheltered back window Wren sees an old man in a headset at the reels while the steel door is bolted.

f_st_alder.event: Alder lets Wren in; he says nobody listens and tonight is only goodbye, with four minutes left.

e_st_alder_send.event: Wren admits nobody can promise Marin listens; Alder speaks live and Marin answers Dad.

e_st_alder_refuse.event: Wren promises Marin is listening; Alder withdraws, plays the goodbye into silence and wipes the tape.

e_st_note.event: Wren says the note was hers; Alder shows it, says Grandpa answered him with two dots for years, and Marin answers.

e_st_wait.event: Wren pounds on the steel door unheard; the lamp goes out as Alder's message plays behind the glass she could have tapped.

f_relay_1.event: Wren uncovers Grandpa's transmitter and weighs sending herself against ringing the radio net.

f_re_rig.event: Wren powers the transmitter and patches the loop through with her voice; the needle's pencil mark sits below a red band.

f_re_boost.event: Sending at the pencil mark, Wren draws a silent carrier and a ringing telephone.

e_re_answer.event: Wren speaks to the carrier; Marin answers and Wren lets the two share the channel.

e_re_neighbor.event: A neighbor and the county net controller relay the message; none are Marin but strangers repeat her name as the loop falls silent.

e_re_fuse.event: Wren turns the power into the red band; the set pops and burns out after ten seconds on the air.

f_re_club.event: The net's emergency line offers press one for danger or leave a message.

f_re_net.event: The duty controller sends Marin's name across the county; a woman west keeps asking and he can patch her through.

e_re_found.event: Patched through, Marin says she read the numbers at seventeen and has listened thirty years without touching the key; Alder answers live.

e_re_log.event: Wren and the controller log twenty-three stations that promise to repeat the message every hour.

e_re_message.event: Wren leaves a message; next morning the controller says a listener west asked after KX every winter for eleven years.

f_help_1.event: Wren must choose whom to wake: the coast guard auxiliary, an old relay man in the address book, or Mrs. Okafor.

f_he_okafor.event: Mrs. Okafor drives Wren to the station and unlocks the back door with a key Alder gave her.

e_he_okafor.event: Okafor makes Alder dial the circled number; Marin answers.

f_he_cg.event: The auxiliary duty officer demands a location then the nature of the emergency.

f_he_act.event: Wren gives location, hazard and time; a crew chief at the station can do only one job before the tide.

e_he_escort.event: The clerk finds Marin's number; the chief puts her through to Alder.

e_he_safe.event: The crew sandbags and powers the station, Alder throws HOLD with four seconds left, and a missing-relative file is opened for Marin.

e_he_dismiss.event: Wren tells the whole story; the officer logs it as a curiosity and the sea floods the station that night.

f_he_colleague.event: Grandpa's address book lists eight transferred relay staff and Ruiz, who stayed and won't talk.

f_he_join.event: Ruiz drives Wren to the station and tells her to stay in the truck.

e_he_complete.event: Wren and Ruiz go in; Ruiz splices a spare cell and Wren dials Marin's number; both men reach for the phone.

e_he_takeover.event: Wren stays in the truck; Ruiz returns near one saying Alder invites her in daylight.

e_he_dead.event: Wren calls the inland numbers until a man names Ruiz; the lamp he watched went out eleven minutes ago.

payoff_sites.shows: The spare battery spliced onto the bare terminals steadies the dying cell.
Without the battery Wren can only nurse the cell, and it dies on the word Marin.
The headset reveals an old recording of a girl calling the operator Dad under the voice.
Alder answers the note with a recorded thank-you to W.
Wren admits the note was hers and Alder shows he kept it.
Mrs. Okafor, told the truth, answers at once and drives Wren to the station with a key.

e_coord_notice.gift: the lesson that a message pinned for a stranger was meant to be taken

e_coord_shed_leave.gift: Grandpa knew about the loop all along and Wren knows where to look next time

e_re_photo.gift: a photograph proving a man lives out there, and a reason to go by the sheltered lane

e_re_cellar.gift: the promise LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, memorized, and a warning about the sea

e_no_letters.gift: the discovery that Grandpa wanted the letters delivered, and a reason to hurry next time

e_no_cards_end.gift: the M card, a clue that someone has been listening in secret

e_no_locked.gift: the slip about two dots every midnight, a clue to what Grandpa sent

e_num_gibberish.gift: the lesson that the one clean fragment was the whole message

e_num_giveup.gift: the lesson to trust a method she can test, and the date she would not circle

e_who_warn.gift: a sharper question: why would a man keep a girl's voice on the air for thirty years

e_list_deadend.gift: the ringed M beside the breakwater, the only mark Grandpa ever ringed twice

e_count_wait.gift: proof that the tide table was right and that trusting it sooner would have mattered

e_st_reunite.gift: Alder hears his daughter on the line as the tape erases, and Wren hands him the phone

e_st_archive.gift: thirty years of tapes saved and Alder deciding to stay

e_st_stabilize.gift: a roomful of people now carrying Alder's thirty years of waiting

e_st_both.gift: the tapes saved and Marin's voice reaching Alder in the same minute

e_st_record.gift: one recorded word, Marin, and the lesson of the spare battery marked JUST IN CASE

e_st_hesitate.gift: the lesson that the straight way across was only thirty yards

e_st_alder_send.gift: Alder speaks live for the first time in thirty years and Marin answers

e_st_alder_refuse.gift: the lesson that an honest not-knowing earns more trust than a false promise

e_st_note.gift: Grandpa's two dots finally answered, and Marin saying she always was there

e_st_wait.gift: the lesson that the window was glass and only six steps away

e_re_answer.gift: Marin on the air, and Wren giving the two of them the channel

e_re_neighbor.gift: a message carried further than the transmitter could throw it, as strangers say Marin's name

e_re_fuse.gift: Grandpa's pencil mark understood: he was not being timid

e_re_found.gift: Marin's own voice saying she has been listening to herself asking her to come home

e_re_log.gift: a hundred pairs of hands on a message that belonged to one man for thirty years

e_re_message.gift: the lesson to press one when a goodbye is at stake

e_he_okafor.gift: Mrs. Okafor makes Alder dial the number he has had for six years

e_he_escort.gift: Marin's number found in four minutes and her father on the line

e_he_safe.gift: the station and tapes saved, and a search begun for Marin

e_he_dismiss.gift: the officer's advice for next time: start with the tide

e_he_complete.gift: three people together at last, and Ruiz letting Alder take the phone

e_he_takeover.gift: an open door in daylight and the lesson that some things are heard from the man himself

e_he_dead.gift: the knowledge that Ruiz was the right call, and that it came too late
